chunks: And upon you be peace. Know, O servants of Allah,

that the God-fearing have taken both the immediate [joys] of this world and the enduring [rewards] of the Hereafter, so they shared with the people of this world in their worldly matters, while the people of this world did not share with them in their Hereafter.

They dwelled in the world in the best manner in which it was dwelled, and consumed it in the best manner in which it was consumed, so they obtained from the world what the opulent obtained, and took from it what the haughty tyrants took,

then they turned away from it with sufficient provision and a profitable trade. They tasted the pleasure of renouncing the world while in this world, and they became certain that they would be neighbors of Allah tomorrow in their Hereafter,
their supplication will not be repelled, nor will their share of pleasure be diminished.

key_terms.آجِلِ الْآخِرَةِ: The enduring/permanent rewards of the Hereafter
key_terms.الزَّادِ الْمُبَلِّغِ: Sufficient provision (spiritual deeds) that carries one to the destination
key_terms.الْمُتَّقِينَ: The God-fearing; those who possess taqwa (God-consciousness)
key_terms.عَاجِلِ الدُّنْيَا: The immediate/transient joys of this world

ai.seo_question: How do the God-fearing balance worldly enjoyment with spiritual preparation for the Hereafter?
ai.summary: In this instruction to Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, Imam Ali (AS) defines the *muttaqun* not as ascetics who reject the world, but as those who master it, enjoying its luxuries like the wealthy while remaining spiritually detached. This concept of 'worldly detachment amidst engagement' ensures that their worldly pleasures do not distract from their ultimate destination, securing a 'profitable transaction' with God. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing material responsibility with spiritual purity, where the believer uses the world as a means to attain proximity to Allah.

en.sayed-ali-raza: that the God-fearing have shared the joys of this transient world as well as the next coming world, for they shared with the people of this world in their worldly matters while their people did not share with them in the matters of the next world.

They lived in this world in the best manner of living and ate the choicest food and consequently they enjoyed herein all that the people with ease of life enjoyed, and secured from it what the haughty and the vain secured.

Then, they departed from it after taking provision enough to take them to the end of their journey and after doing a profitable transaction. They tasted the pleasure of renouncing the world in this world, and they firmly believed that on the coming day in their next life they would be neighbours of Allāh,
where their call would not be repulsed nor would their share of pleasure be small.
